transactions.detail: Memphis (MEM) fully guaranteed $9 million salary for 2026-27
transactions.why: His offer sheet is reported as 3yr/$30M, which is $26.1M of base plus $1.35M a year of unlikely incentives; the signings feed carries the $26.1M base. Back-solved with standard 5% RAISES that gives a 2026-27 of $8,285,714, but the deal steps DOWN after year one — Spotrac's cap tables have him at $9,000,000 for 2026-27 and $8,550,000 for 2027-28 (non-guaranteed, with $1,282,500 of unlikely incentives), and 9.0 + 8.55 + 8.55 is $26.1M exactly. (This note said 9.0 / 8.7 / 8.4 until Oct 2 2026, a guess at the shape that the 2027-28 filing corrected.) A descending shape is legal (Art. II §5(b) allows an 8% decline) and it is what was filed, so the year-one figure is stated here for STATED_SALARY rather than inferred. Our own resolvedOfferSheetsNote already said 'Y1 $9M guaranteed'; nothing was reading it.

transactions.detail: Waived by Sacramento (SAC) - leaves behind $10 million in dead cap
transactions.why: Sacramento waived him Jul 6 2026 keeping a $10M guarantee, which roster-corrections carried as a waivedFreeAgents entry — a shape that only describes an UNSIGNED waived player. When he signed with Denver on Aug 21 his row moved to DEN with the new minimum and Sacramento's $10M vanished from the league's books entirely. He is now the ACTIVE_LATER case Jonathan Isaac already documents: the old team's charge needs its own dead row beside the new deal, and STATED_DEAD_CAP builds one from a Release row that states the amount. This is that row. UPDATED Sep 1: Sacramento stretched the $10M at the Aug 31 deadline (Hoops Rumors, Aug 28), and Spotrac rewrote the Jul 6 feed row to 'via Stretch Provision'. This row still supplies the AMOUNT; the feed's row supplies the stretch flag, and STATED_DEAD_CAP spreads the $10M to $3,333,333 a season through 2028-29.

Cross-check: $7,660,317 from Dallas plus his new Miami salary against the $17,460,317 he walked away from is the ~$3.5M net loss the reporting describes.

transactions.detail: Waived by Memphis Grizzlies (MEM) via Buyout - leaves behind $6.343013 million in dead cap
transactions.why: He was owed $7,021,895 for 2026-27 when Memphis waived him on Oct 2, three weeks after taking him from New Orleans. Spotrac files it as a buyout with $678,882 in cap savings, which is exactly a full season of two-way pay (half the $1,357,763 rookie minimum), and Hoops Rumors (Oct 6) puts Memphis at about $6.3MM after he signed his two-way in Chicago. It is a giveback, not set-off: Art. XXVII only offsets half of what a new deal pays above the minimum, and a two-way pays less than the minimum. $7,021,895 − $678,882 = $6,343,013. Without this row the waive charged Memphis the full $7.02M.
